summary: This document sets out requirements for Content Distribution Network Interconnection. As more providers build their own CDNs, they need ways to deliver content across each other's networks, for example when a user is outside the footprint of the CDN contracted by the content provider.

eli5.summary: If your favorite store has no shop in your town, it could use another company's trucks. This RFC lists what is needed so different delivery networks can hand content to each other.

questions: what is an upstream cdn and downstream cdn
subtitle: The requirements for letting separate content delivery networks cooperate as one delivery platform.

tldr.problem: Content may need to cross several separately run content delivery networks (CDNs) to reach an end user, and those networks had no standard way to work together.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists prioritized requirements, tagged HIGH, MED or LOW, for five interfaces: control, request routing redirection, footprint and capabilities advertisement, metadata and logging, plus generic and security requirements.
tldr.outcome: It is the requirements input for the solution and interfaces the CDNI working group was chartered to specify; it does not define the protocols itself.

facts.label: Interfaces
facts.value: Control, Request Routing (FCI, RI), Metadata, Logging

today: RFC 7337 is an Informational RFC published in August 2014, and the metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It states requirements for the CDNI interfaces rather than defining protocols; the framework it builds on is RFC 7336.

sections.title: Why CDNs Need to Interconnect
sections.content:
Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) reduce delivery cost for cacheable content, improve quality of experience and increase robustness. Existing CDN providers are scaling up, and many network service providers (NSPs) and enterprise service providers (ESPs) are deploying their own CDNs.

Subject to the policy of the Content Service Provider (CSP), content should be deliverable to an end user regardless of location or attachment network. That creates a need to interconnect previously standalone CDNs so they behave as a single delivery infrastructure. This document gives the requirements for the Content Distribution Network Interconnection (CDNI) solution. The problem is outlined in RFC 6707, the use cases in RFC 6770 and the framework in RFC 7336.

To meet the working group's timelines, each requirement is tagged {HIGH}, {MED} or {LOW}. HIGH is essential and has to be met even if it delays the solution. MED has to be met unless that would cause delay. LOW will be attempted as long as it does not block the others.
sections.eli5: Many small delivery companies want to work like one big one. This document is the wish list, sorted from must-have to nice-to-have.

sections.title: The CDNI Model and Interfaces
sections.content:
An Upstream CDN hands work to a Downstream CDN. Between them sit four interfaces inside the scope of CDNI:

  • The Control interface (CI) bootstraps the other interfaces and handles pre-positioning, revalidating and purging of content and metadata.
  • The Request Routing interface decides which CDN, and optionally which Surrogate, serves a user. It bundles the Footprint and Capabilities Advertisement interface (FCI, asynchronous) and the Request Routing Redirection interface (RI, synchronous).
  • The Metadata interface (MI) carries data that governs delivery, such as geo-blocking, availability windows and access control.
  • The Logging interface (LI) exchanges activity logs, in real time for monitoring and offline for analytics and billing.

The definitive model is in RFC 7336; this RFC replicates it for convenience.
sections.eli5: The companies need four kinds of conversation: how to set up, who delivers to which house, the special rules for each parcel, and the record of what was delivered.

sections.title: Generic and Control Requirements
sections.content:
The generic requirements (GEN-1 to GEN-13) say the solution should reuse existing IETF protocols, and must not require changes to the User Agent or to a CSP that delivers through a single CDN. It must not depend on exposing intra-CDN information such as Surrogate topology or cached content, must support HTTP for delivery and acquisition, must prevent looping of information exchange, and must support HTTP Adaptive Streaming. Cascaded redirection (CDN1 to CDN2 to CDN3) and arbitrary CDN topologies are MED priority.

The Control interface requirements (CI-1 to CI-12) cover purging. The Upstream CDN must be able to ask the Downstream CDN, including cascaded ones, to delete objects, and only objects that pertain to the requesting Upstream CDN may be purged. The Downstream CDN must report completion with a success or failure indication. Pre-positioning of metadata and content, and bootstrapping the other interfaces, are lower priority.
sections.eli5: Nobody should have to change how they already work, nobody should reveal private warehouse details, and a company may only throw away its own parcels.

sections.title: Request Routing and Capability Requirements
sections.content:
For Request Routing Redirection (RI-1 to RI-15), the interface must support efficient routing for both small objects, where a DNS-style mode trades accuracy for lower load, and large objects, where a per-request HTTP-style decision is justified. It must support both recursive and iterative routing. The Upstream CDN must be able to send the Downstream CDN enough information to process the query, and the Downstream CDN must reply with an accept or reject status plus redirection information. Per-chunk routing of HTTP Adaptive Streaming is HIGH priority.

The Footprint and Capabilities Advertisement interface (FCI-1 to FCI-7) lets the Downstream CDN tell the Upstream CDN whether it can take more requests, and describe its footprint, supported content types and delivery protocols, resources and affinities. Advertised information must be extensible.
sections.eli5: When a customer asks for a parcel, one company asks another, "Can you deliver this, and how?" The second must be able to say yes or no and explain why.

sections.title: Metadata and Logging Requirements
sections.content:
The Metadata interface (MI-1 to MI-22) must let the Upstream CDN give the Downstream CDN metadata with inter-CDN scope, in both dynamic and pre-positioned acquisition models. It must say where to acquire content, support removal of obsolete metadata, attach metadata to a single object or an object set, and support inheritance where more specific metadata overrides broader metadata. Conflicting metadata with overlapping scope must be prevented or handled deterministically. Examples of delivery policy are geo-blocking, availability windows and delegation whitelists or blacklists. A Content Collection ID groups related content such as adaptive streaming chunks.

The Logging interface (LI-1 to LI-17) must reliably transfer logs, log deliveries and incomplete deliveries, support batch and offline exchange, and define a log file format and a transport. Near-real-time logging is MED. Logging should offer optional privacy protection, such as anonymizing the IP address.
sections.eli5: Each parcel can come with instructions like "only deliver to this town" or "only before Friday". The delivering company also keeps a diary and shares it, without naming the customers if asked.

sections.title: Security Requirements
sections.content:
Section 9 holds the security requirements, and the Security Considerations section simply refers to it. All CDNI interfaces must support secure operation over unsecured IP connectivity, including authentication, confidentiality, integrity protection and protection against spoofing and replay (SEC-1, HIGH).

The solution must also protect against denial-of-service attacks, including spoofed delivery requests sent directly to a Downstream CDN that pretend to have been redirected by an Upstream CDN (SEC-2, HIGH). Two MED requirements say a Downstream CDN should be able to tell which Upstream CDN redirected a request, and an Upstream CDN should be able to confirm that a log record matches a redirection it made.
sections.eli5: The companies must be sure who they are talking to, and nobody can pretend to be a partner to get free deliveries.

items.title: Control (CI)
items.text: Bootstraps others; pre-position, revalidate and purge.

items.title: Request Routing (FCI, RI)
items.text: Chooses which CDN or Surrogate serves a user.

items.title: Metadata (MI)
items.text: Delivery rules such as geo-blocking and windows.

items.label: High Priority
items.desc: Essential; must be met even if it delays a deployable solution.

items.label: Medium Priority
items.desc: Important; met unless it would delay a deployable solution.

items.label: Low Priority
items.desc: Useful; attempted if it does not block the others.
